KarteaViewFactory

class KarteaViewFactory(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: GameViewFactoryProtocol

Build the KarTEA register screens.

For each screen, create the view, create the controller with the services and connect both (view.bind(controller)). Views and controllers neither create each other nor create services.

Notes

Each list screen receives ONE instance of each service, shared with the edit dialogs opened from it. The instances are deliberately not global: the game runs in another process and writes the same CSV files (phase/level, session); a list opened after a match must read the data again, not an old cache.

static create_player_config_edit_view(parent=None, config=None, service=None, phase_service=None)[source]

Create the player configuration edit screen.

Parameters:
parentQDialog | None, optional

Parent widget of the dialog.

configPlayerKarteaConfig | None, optional

Config to edit; None opens the screen to create a new one.

servicePlayerKarteaConfigService | None, optional

Config service to share (e.g. the list screen’s). Created if None.

phase_serviceKarteaPhaseService | None, optional

Phase service to share. Created if None.

Returns:
PlayerKarteaConfigEditView

The view, already bound to its controller.

Notes

Without services (dialog opened outside the list), the screen creates its own.

static create_player_config_list_view(parent=None, player_config_edit_view=None)[source]

Create the player configuration list screen.

Parameters:
parentQObject | None, optional

Parent of the view.

player_config_edit_viewEditViewFactory | None, optional

Factory of the edit dialog. Defaults to create_player_config_edit_view.

Returns:
PlayerKarteaConfigListView

The view, already bound to its controller.

Notes

Creates one PlayerKarteaConfigService and one KarteaPhaseService and shares them with every edit dialog opened from the list. They are passed only as the keyword arguments the edit factory accepts, so a factory with the plain (parent, config) signature also works.
